item.title: Trezor Warns of Suspected Hardware Implant in One of Its Wallets Sold by CryptoBilis
item.author: The Hacker News
item.description:

From The Hacker News.

A Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallet bought from the reseller CryptoBilis has an extra circuit board that sends out the recovery phrase over a mobile network, a customer has reported. Trezor has not yet examined the device. It is telling everyone who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to move their funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase. item.title: Ask Ethan: What should you do when a respected theory is false?
item.author: Big Think
item.description:
Why: Ethan Siegel on how science should respond when a respected theory turns out to be wrong. (score 7)

From Big Think.

At every point in our quest to understand the world and universe — the one around us and the one within us — we can only start based on what we know and can imagine at present. We are biased by what we know and what we’re ignorant of, and we’re also influenced by the range of experiences that we’re aware of. item.title: The 3 great origin mysteries: The universe, life, and consciousness
item.author: Big Think
item.description:
Why: Paul Davies on the three great origin mysteries: the universe, life, and consciousness. (score 7)

From Big Think.

Physicist and cosmologist Paul Davies, author of The Demon in the Machine, argues that the deepest mystery of life’s origin is how chemistry came to write its own code. Davies traces the question from Aristotle and Schrödinger’s “aperiodic crystal” to Maxwell’s demon, Michael Levin’s two-headed flatworms, and the possibility of a shadow biosphere hiding on Earth. This video The 3 great origin mysteries: The universe, life, and consciousness is featured on Big Think .
